No.987/2021 dated 27.01.2024.

sentences.text:
3. The undisputed facts of the case are as under:
(i) The claimant was aged around 6 years by the date of accident.
NC: 2025:KHC-D:15077 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100106 of 2024 HC-KAR (ii) The claimant was hit by a car which was insured with the Insurance Company as on the date of accident, due to which she sustained fracture of left tibia.
(iii) The claimant took treatment as inpatient at District Hospital, Chitradurga and thereafter at Aarogya Hospital, Huvina Hadagali.

4. Arguing the matter, Sri Subhash J. Baddi, learned counsel representing the insurance company states that the Tribunal though assessed the disability in respect of whole body as 25% and also discussed the law laid down regarding grant of compensation to minors in the case between Master Mallikarjun And Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & Another1, yet without following the said decision awarded whimsical and exorbitant amount as compensation and therefore the present appeal is filed.
Learned counsel submits that the interest granted on the awarded sum is also on higher side. 2014(14) SCC 396 NC: 2025:KHC-D:15077 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100106 of 2024 HC-KAR 5.

Opposing the said submission, Sri Santosh B. Kanal learned counsel for the claimant submits that the disability as assessed by PW-2 is 75% and therefore the sum granted as compensation is highly justifiable.

6. Having discussed the merits of the case at length and subjecting the evidence of PW-2 to scrutiny,
the Tribunal came to a conclusion that the disability in respect of whole body can be considered as 25%.
7.
The contents of Ex.P.18-Disability Certificate go to show that the total permanent physical disability in respect of left ankle is 70%.
Ex.P.18 is silent in respect of disability with regard to whole body.

Admittedly, the claimant sustained fracture to left tibia and in respect of left lower limb alone,
the disability was assessed.

Hence, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal did not err in assessing the disability in respect of whole body as 25%.
8.

As rightly put forth by learned counsel for the Insurance Company, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex NC: 2025:KHC-D:15077 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100106 of 2024 HC-KAR Court in Master Mallikarjun (supra), where the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, the compensation which the claimant is entitled to receive is Rs.3,00,000/-.

sentences.text:
Thus, the total sum which the claimant is entitled to receive as compensation is Rs.5,30,780/- (3,00,000 +
1,65,780 + 40,000 + 25,000).
The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.8,05,780/- as compensation.
Thus, the amount granted in excess is Rs.2,75,000/- (Rs.8,05,780 - Rs.5,30,780).
Also as rightly put forth by learned counsel for the Insurance Company, the interest which can be awarded on the compensation granted should have been 6% only.
NC: 2025:KHC-D:15077 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100106 of 2024 HC-KAR 9.

Thus, both the appeals are disposed of with the following:
ORDER (i) MFA No.102057/2024 is allowed in part.

(ii) The compensation that is granted by the  Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-XIII,
 H.B.Halli through orders in M.V.C.
 No.987/2021 dated 27.01.2024 is  reduced by Rs.2,50,000/-.
(iii) The sum awarded as compensation shall  carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

(iv) The appeal in M.F.A.CROB.
No.100106/2024 stands dismissed.
(v) Amount if any in deposit, be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal immediately.
